marks.gloss_en: ורבי יוחנן מאי טעמא לא קא חשיב להא? -- why does R' Yochanan count three and omit the key of livelihood?
אמר לך: גשמים היינו פרנסה (= p_geshamim_hainu_parnasa, attributed to R' Yochanan)
in the West they say: also the key of livelihood
the key of the resurrection, whence? -- as it is written: 'and you shall know that I am the Lord when I open your graves' (Ezek 37:13)
תא שמע, דאמר רבי אבהו: לא למדה רבי אליעזר אלא מלולב -- the ta-shema is R' Abbahu's dictum itself, hence no separate source prop
R' Abbahu learned it [that R' Eliezer derived from the lulav] as a received tradition
מאי היא? דתניא: ... רבי אליעזר אומר משעת נטילת לולב -- the baraita behind R' Abbahu's dictum (no support kind names a דתניא identification; svara stands in)
R' Eliezer: one mentions rain from the time of taking the lulav
דאמר מר: ומנחתם ונסכיהם -- אפילו בלילה (a cited dictum; svara stands in for the missing kind)
if from the lulav: as the lulav is by day, so the mention begins by day
והתנן: יצא ניסן וירדו גשמים -- סימן קללה הם (no support kind names והתנן; svara stands in)

אמר לך רבי יהושע: every day is the resurrection's time (= p_tchiya_kol_yoma_zimnei); is every rainfall rain's time? (= p_geshamim_lav_kol_zman) -- והתנן: rain after Nisan is a sign of curse (= p_mishnah_yatza_nisan)
but rain -- is every time it comes its time?!
אמר לו רבי יהושע: והלא גשמים בחג אינו אלא סימן קללה -- why mention rain at a time when rain is a curse?
אף אני לא אמרתי לשאול אלא להזכיר (= p_eliezer_lehazkir_lo_lishol), as the resurrection is mentioned all year though it comes only in its time (= p_eliezer_ketchiyat_hametim)
R' Yehoshua: but rain on the Chag is nothing but a sign of curse
שפיר קאמר ליה רבי אליעזר לרבי יהושע! -- R' Eliezer's resurrection analogy answers R' Yehoshua well
granted the resurrection is mentioned [daily], for every day is its time
אימא תרוייהו דחמרא! -- say both libations are of wine
סבר לה כרבי יהודה בן בתירה, דאמר רמיזי מיא (= p_akiva_kerybb)
the stam: R' Akiva holds like RYBB, who said water is alluded [so the second libation is of water]
R' Eliezer (mishna): one mentions [the might of the rains] from the first Festival day of the Chag
R' Eliezer: since these four species come only to appease for water, and as they cannot be without water so the world cannot be without water
R' Yehuda ben Beteira: one mentions [rain] on the second day of the Chag
RYBB (baraita): on the second day it says 'veniskeiheM', on the sixth 'unsakhEha', on the seventh 'kemishpataM'
there is mem, yod, mem -- here is 'water': from here an allusion to the water libation from the Torah
the stam: when [the libations] are alluded in the verse, it is on the second day that they are alluded; therefore on the second day we mention
R' Akiva: as it says on the sixth 'and its libations' -- the verse speaks of two libations, one of water and one of wine
